title.zh: Picard 磁通状态相对残差

summary: Measure the Euclidean change between successive two-dimensional flux states relative to the previous state, with scaled arithmetic and a small denominator floor.

identity.relation: previous and next flux states to a relative Euclidean change diagnostic
identity.definition: Compute ||psi_next-psi_previous||_2 / max(||psi_previous||_2, 1e-30 Wb) using the largest absolute input magnitude as an arithmetic scale. A zero-valued pair returns zero. Reject a zero scaled denominator or a nonfinite final ratio; representability at extreme subnormal magnitudes is not guaranteed.
identity.model: discrete relative L2 flux-state change for a Picard stopping criterion
identity.coordinates: both arrays indexed [Z,R], with no interpretation of physical spacings by this Operator
identity.boundary: All grid entries participate equally; no spatial boundary or active-cell mask is used.
assumptions: Both arrays represent the same flux quantity in Wb on matching [Z,R] samples.
The 1e-30 Wb norm floor is a numerical convention and not a physical reference scale; Wb/rad states cannot be assumed interchangeable with this Wb contract.

inputs.name: psi_previous
inputs.description: Flux state before a Picard update.
inputs.constraints: Two-dimensional and exactly same shape as psi_next; may be zero.

inputs.name: psi_next
inputs.description: Flux state after a Picard update.
inputs.constraints: Two-dimensional and exactly same shape as psi_previous; may be zero.

outputs.name: residual
outputs.constraints: Nonnegative finite result when representable; zero for two zero states or identical states.

preconditions: The two states use identical flux units, grid coordinates and shape.
supported: A numerical Picard stopping diagnostic for finite two-dimensional arrays, including selected very large and very small magnitudes.
excluded: A physical equilibrium residual or an error against an independent source oracle.
Area weighting, mask weighting or arbitrary tensor rank.
A guarantee that every finite input pair yields a representable finite relative ratio, or that a Wb/rad graph state can be passed without a science-approved convention.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for unequal shapes, non-two-dimensional arrays or nonfinite entries.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError for a zero scaled denominator or nonfinite final ratio; other NumPy conversion or arithmetic failures propagate. Extreme subnormal scaling is not guaranteed to preserve the mathematical ratio.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this Operator only measures one state change.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping is returned on failure.

provenance.lineage_summary: The current SciRel implementation and direct tests were compared with the historical Pleiades development mapping and pending intake candidate; source text matched. Historical admission labels and intake r81-v1 do not establish current expert approval or qualified D1 delivery. The free-boundary graph consumes this diagnostic, but its Wb convention does not approve Wb/rad cross-asset wiring.
source_kinds: historical Pleiades development descriptor and migration mapping
current SciRel implementation and direct numerical regression tests

example.description: Doubling a 3-4 flux state produces a unit relative change; the unchanged state has zero residual.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.diagnostics import compute_picard_flux_residual
previous = np.array([[3.0, 4.0]])
assert compute_picard_flux_residual(previous, previous)['residual'] == 0.0
assert np.isclose(compute_picard_flux_residual(previous, 2*previous)['residual'], 1.0)
example.expected: The unchanged residual is 0 and the doubled-state residual is 1.

scope: Large and small finite numerical boundaries, including changes whose unscaled subtraction overflows.
Wrong-rank or mismatched shapes and nonfinite input entries are rejected.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct numerical tests cover selected finite extremes and the formula, but not physical equilibrium convergence, arbitrary underflow behavior or expert recognition.
known_limitations: The denominator floor changes the relative ratio when the previous-state norm is below 1e-30 Wb.
At the smallest subnormal magnitudes, 1e-30/scale may overflow during scaling, so the returned zero need not equal the mathematical ratio.
The Wb floor does not scale invariantly when reinterpreting Wb/rad states; no conversion or direct graph wiring is approved here.
The scalar does not test Maxwell or pressure-force equations.
Public distribution licensing and expert recognition remain pending.
